header.name: Fields and Waves
header.description: This is an introductory course to electrodynamics (along with electrostatics and magnetostatics). This course will serve as a foundational course for students interested in working in RF and micro-wave, millimeter wave and optical systems.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to execute vector calculus operations (gradient, divergence, curl, line, surface and volume integrals) in Cartesian and curvilinear coordinates

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to use Coulomb's law, Gauss's law and Poisson's equation to solve for electric field, flux density and potentials for point, line, surface and volume charge distributions

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to use Biot Savart's law and Ampere's law to solve for magnetic field and flux density

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze Maxwell's equations of time- harmonic fields to describe electromagnetic wave propagation in different media and across boundaries

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze electromagnetic wave propagation through simple transmission lines

lecture_topics: Electromagnetic waves propagation - the Helmholtz wave equation
electromagnetic waves in vaccuum and in matter
reflection and transmission at normal incidence
reflection and transmission at oblique incidence
Transmission lines equations and parameters (time domain and frequency domain)

resources.title: Introduction to Electrodynamics, Third Edition, David J. Griffiths
Engineering Electromagnetics, Eigth Edition, Hayt, Buck and Akhtar
Principles of Electromagnetics 4th Edition, Mathew N. O. Sadiku.
